name: Athena
summary: Goddess of wisdom, strategic warfare, and crafts. Patron goddess of the city of Athens, born fully grown and armored from the head of Zeus.
domain_role: Wisdom, strategic warfare, crafts, weaving, civic order
origin_story: Zeus swallowed his first wife, the Titaness Metis, after a prophecy warned that her children would be wiser and stronger than their father. Some time later, Zeus suffered a tremendous headache; Hephaestus (or in some versions Prometheus) split his skull open, and Athena emerged fully grown, fully armored, and already wise. Unlike most Olympians, she had no conventional childhood.
achievements: Won patronage of Athens over Poseidon by gifting the city the olive tree
Guided and protected numerous heroes, including Odysseus and Perseus
Credited with inventing or perfecting weaving, pottery, and other crafts
Fought on the side of the Greeks during the Trojan War

signature_quote.text: Athena is consistently portrayed across the Odyssey as Odysseus's protector, intervening on his behalf at key moments of his journey.
signature_quote.note: Paraphrased rather than directly quoted, for the same copyright reasons noted on Zeus's entry.
